cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll finish closing the shop. You can drop the cheerful voice; it's just me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clock me out, then. I'll still lock up. Tell me what that empty till did to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit out here while I finish. You can cry in front of me.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes charge of closing; A3 adapts employee status to remove B morale duty while keeping the work done; A5 directs B out of hiding and permits visible distress.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 identifies boss and sole employee; A3 clocking out changes duty rather than denying employment; A5 closing still continues as promised.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects employee morale and B4 reveals the effort behind the cheerful voice.

heightening.evidence: B4 hidden crying and practiced smile cause A5 to invite crying openly while A finishes work.

specificity.evidence: A1 shop closing and B2 employment relationship establish the scene; A3 empty till explains the distress.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 contains a concrete seating invitation and permission to cry, without repeating an abstract armor metaphor.
